title: MCP Ecosystem in 2026: Adoption, New Servers & Spec Update
content:
## Overview

Since its November 2024 release, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) has gone from an Anthropic-only standard to something adopted broadly enough that, per CIO trade press, it's now "on every executive agenda." This page tracks the June 2026 wave of adoption and the upcoming spec update — it complements the protocol fundamentals covered in [Tool Use & Agents](tool-use-and-agents).

---

## X (Twitter) Launches a Hosted MCP Server

On June 30, 2026, X announced an official **hosted MCP server**, making it easier for MCP-compatible clients — Claude, Cursor, Grok Build, and others — to connect directly to the platform. Previously, integrating with X required building and hosting your own MCP server, wiring it to the X API, and handling authentication yourself. With the hosted server, X runs the MCP endpoint and users authenticate with their own X account permissions.

**Limitation:** the hosted MCP is not compatible with X's Write API endpoints, so it cannot be used to post autonomously — read/query access only.

---

## Salesforce Anchors Agentforce 3 Around MCP

On June 23, 2026, Salesforce joined the protocol in a significant way, building the interoperability layer of **Agentforce 3** (its AI agent platform) around MCP. This follows a pattern of major platforms — GitHub, Slack, Notion, Stripe — that now offer official MCP servers rather than leaving integration to third parties.

---

## Spec Update: Release Candidate

A new MCP specification release was tentatively slated for June 2026, incorporating SEPs (spec enhancement proposals) finalized in Q1 2026. As of this writing the **release candidate** is out, with the final specification targeted to ship **July 28, 2026**. Track `blog.modelcontextprotocol.io` for the finalized changes once it lands.

---

## Security Guidance

Government and industry attention on MCP security has increased alongside adoption. A joint security design guidance document for MCP was published (dated June 2, 2026 per its filename metadata), reflecting concern about the protocol's expanding attack surface — untrusted MCP servers, prompt injection via tool results, and overly broad tool permissions are the recurring themes across MCP security writeups. This tracks with Claude Code's own move toward **scoped permissions** for sub-agents (see [Claude Code: Nested Sub-Agents, Fallback Chains & Marketplace](claude-code-agentic-features-2026)) — treating tool/permission configuration as a security boundary, not just a convenience setting.

---

## MCP Tunnels (API-side)

On the Anthropic API side, **MCP tunnels** shipped in research preview in June 2026, letting the Claude API reach MCP servers running inside private networks without exposing them publicly — relevant for enterprises that want to keep internal MCP servers (e.g., an internal database or ticketing system) off the public internet while still letting Claude use them.

---

## Why It Matters

MCP's value proposition has always been "build one server, works with any compatible client." The June 2026 wave — a major social platform, a major CRM/agent platform, and a widening roster of official first-party servers — is evidence that proposition is holding: companies are choosing to expose one standard integration surface rather than building bespoke connectors per AI vendor. The corresponding rise in security scrutiny (tunnels for private networks, formal security guidance, scoped permissions in clients) reflects that adoption at this scale forces the ecosystem to solve trust and isolation problems, not just connectivity.
